items.title: Specification / notes
items.text: The property is 100 ft wide (street side, south) by 140 ft deep. The dashed red rectangle on the plan is the property line. Two-story house with an attached garage on the east side; the house is beige siding with a dark gray roof. Keep it simple for this first test: transcribe the house, driveway, front walk, lawns, beds and all plants shown in the legend.

items.title: Answers to round 1 questions
items.text: Yes, the garage is a two-car garage facing the street (south). Yes, the three gray circles in the front tree bed are boulders. Location: Columbus, Ohio (lat 39.96, lon -83.0, UTC-4 in summer); north is up on the plan. There is a 6 ft wood privacy fence along the back and both sides of the backyard, from the back corners of the house to the rear property line. Please run the validate and check commands this time and confirm the overlay lines up.

items.title: Option B change
items.text: Option B: make the backyard patio about 50% larger by extending it 10 ft further into the yard (north). Everything else stays the same as the parent design.

rounds.summary: Option B overlays the parent design and extends the backyard flagstone patio 10 ft north (far edge moved from y≈95-100 to y≈105-110 ft), growing it from roughly 600 sq ft to roughly 920 sq ft (about +50%). The seat wall, hosta planting and stepping-stone path that sat on the old north edge were shifted 10 ft north with it. Everything else is inherited from the parent.
notes: Validate reports no errors. The only warning, that street-tree-w and street-tree-e fall outside the property boundary, is inherited from the parent; those trees are in the street strip.

The plan-check overlay matches the house, garage, driveway, walk, beds and fence. The plan drawing still shows the original patio, seat wall and hostas, so the new patio extends past the drawn patio by design, and the shifted seat wall and hostas sit slightly north of their drawn positions.
I interpreted 'extend 10 ft north' as moving the whole north edge of the patio 10 ft, keeping its angled corner shape, rather than adding a separate rectangle.
The accent maple and patio bed on the east side were left where they are, and the patio's east edge (x=70) is unchanged.
questions: Should the seat wall and hostas move north with the larger patio (as done here), or stay at their original locations?

issues.message: 2 plant(s) outside the property boundary: street-tree-e, street-tree-w
